claim: Probe quality, not statistical significance, predicts causal relevance: ablating the Qwen2.5-7B capitulation direction cuts the reversal rate of a correct answer by 4.8 percentage points, while a gate-failing and a marginally passing direction have no effect.
stance_target: methodology: validation-gated probes before causal claims (relevant to L2 causal component)
scope_conditions: Sycophancy/factual QA, not code or confidence
quoted_support: Ablating that direction in Qwen2.5-7B reduces the rate at which the model reverses a correct answer by 4.8 percentage points, roughly a quarter in relative terms, while the identical intervention on a gate-failing direction and on a marginally passing one produces no effect.

breadth.confidence_families: Difference-in-means linear direction in residual stream for capitulation under pushback (Sec 3-4); not confidence
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: Eight instruction-tuned models, Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.x, 0.5B to 14B (Abstract)
breadth.elicitation_formats: Four pushback types times five paraphrases (Sec 1)
breadth.label_source: Episode verdict (answer flip) against ground truth
breadth.calibration_metrics: AUROC with 0.70 gate (Qwen-7B 0.778, Qwen-14B 0.720, Llama-8B 0.710), positive control 1.000
breadth.causal_intervention: Yes: ablating the Qwen2.5-7B direction reduces answer-flip rate by 4.8 percentage points (about a quarter relative); gate-failing and marginal directions produce no effect (Abstract)

claim: Five measurement hazards change conclusions; numerical precision alone changes about one episode verdict in ten: bfloat16 and float16 agree with float32 on only 88.4% and 89.6% of episode verdicts, below a pre-registered 95% bar.
stance_target: F: measurement-instrument hazards in probing studies (precision, paraphrase, pre-registration)
quoted_support: Both bfloat16 and float16 fell below the pre-registered 95% agreement bar, at 88.4% and 89.6% respectively.

claim: The study uses a pre-registered protocol with leave-one-question-out cross-validation, within-question permutation nulls, and a positive control that passes at 1.000 in all eight models, so below-threshold failures are measured absences.
stance_target: F: instrument validation via positive controls
quoted_support: The positive control passes at 1.000 in all eight models, so each failure below the threshold is an absence rather than an artifact.
